evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the stakeholder need (create game with name/description) without prescribing concrete UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific invitation/delivery mechanism (providing a URL) rather than just the need to invite estimators.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete UI widget (a single multi-line text field) instead of the underlying need to start a round with an item.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need (view items) without prescribing specific UI or technical solutions.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the desired capability (select an item) without unnecessary implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to add items without prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the stakeholder need to edit items; no concrete implementation is imposed.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the need to remove items without prescribing how deletion should be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired behavior (show estimates) but does not prescribe UI widgets or implementation techniques.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific algorithmic solution (use the average) rather than stating the stakeholder need for an accepted estimate.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Specifies automatic field-filling behavior and a concrete UI field, imposing implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's need to record the agreed estimate without prescribing how the UI or system must implement it.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: States the capability needed (re-estimate) without mandating a specific technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete data-source/format (spreadsheet) as the mechanism for importing rather than the need to bulk-add stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes the exact mechanism (copy/paste from a spreadsheet) rather than expressing the higher-level need to quickly add stories.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's need to find past games without dictating implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the need to view transcripts but does not prescribe specific formats or UI controls.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete export format (HTML) rather than stating the need to save a transcript.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a particular export format (CSV), imposing an implementation choice instead of the stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to remove games and associated data without prescribing storage or deletion mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Lists required account data (fields) which is a stakeholder requirement rather than prescribing UI widgets or low-level technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Specifies credential-based login as a user need; this is a domain-appropriate requirement rather than a low-level technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to update account information without prescribing technical or UI solutions.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the user's need for account deletion without mandating specific implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: States a user-visible requirement (local timezone display) rather than prescribing particular technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete delivery mechanism (email) for password reminders instead of the higher-level need to recover access.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific estimation scales (concrete solution choices) rather than stating the need to choose an estimation scale.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Specifies an operational constraint (max participants) which is a valid stakeholder requirement, not a low-level implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Includes a specific joining mechanism (using a URL to access a page) which prescribes an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: States the user's need to view the item without mandating UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the capability to view items without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired visibility of actions (who has estimated) without specifying UI controls or backend mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: States a timing/visibility requirement rather than prescribing UI widgets or technical internals.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Uses domain terms (cards) to express when changes are allowed; does not mandate technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes an informational need (view prior estimates) without prescribing solutions or mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: States the requirement to identify estimators and their estimates without specifying implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a functional capability (a visible timer) rather than prescribing low-level implementation or UI widget details.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired automatic behavior for a feature (timer reset) without imposing technical solutions.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: States a navigation need without prescribing UI widgets or technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a consistent presentation requirement (card order) but not a concrete technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the allowed user action (change estimate) without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete UI presentation details (small thumbnail, placement) rather than the stakeholder need for personal identification.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific technical standards/technologies (XHTML, CSS) as an implementation choice rather than a stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a documentation need (definitions) without dictating technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a low-level implementation detail (creating database indexes) rather than the performance need itself.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes support for specific browser versions (implementation/platform choices) instead of stating accessibility/compatibility needs at a higher level.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a stakeholder need for accessibility; although it references a guideline, it states a quality goal rather than low-level implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: States a non-functional performance requirement (responsiveness) without mandating implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete technical/encoding choice (Unicode) rather than the higher-level need to support multiple languages or character sets.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user-facing requirement about URL clarity without prescribing low-level technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the need for helpful error pages (a UX requirement) rather than implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a privacy requirement (non-identifiable storage) without prescribing specific anonymization techniques or storage formats.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need to view usage metrics without prescribing concrete dashboard technologies or formats.
